newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea steps in again, sells dlrs at 865.50.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea steps in again, sells dlrs at 865.50.

text.p: The Bank of Korea intervened again in the interbank market in mid-afternooon trading on Thursday, selling dollars at around 865.50 to slow the local currency's fall against the U.S. unit, dealers said.
But the bank denied the action, as it routinely does.
The Bank of Korea came in at around 0528 GMT when the won hit the lowest level since a market average system was introduced in March 1990, dealers said.
Demand for the dollar has been rising in line with the increasing import deals, they said.
Traders said the won was expected to decline further if not for the central bank's support, traders said.
The won is currently trading at 864.00.
